reference.source: Murray & Nadel's Textbook of Respiratory Medicine
clinicalPearls: The second most common idiopathic interstitial pneumonia; more often affects middle-aged women and non-smokers.
Strongly associated with connective tissue disease, particularly systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis and Sjögren syndrome, and may be its first manifestation.
Idiopathic NSIP is a diagnosis of exclusion made only after a thorough search for connective tissue disease, drug exposure and hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
Two histological subtypes exist: cellular (predominantly inflammatory, better prognosis) and fibrotic (worse prognosis).
HRCT shows bilateral, symmetrical, basal-predominant ground-glass opacity with fine reticulation and traction bronchiectasis; relative subpleural sparing is characteristic.
Honeycombing is absent or minimal, which helps distinguish NSIP from the UIP pattern of IPF.
Temporal uniformity on histology, with all areas of the same apparent age, contrasts with the spatial and temporal heterogeneity of UIP.
Unlike IPF, disease commonly responds to corticosteroids with or without steroid-sparing immunosuppression.
reference.pathophysiology: NSIP is characterised by a temporally uniform interstitial process combining varying proportions of chronic inflammation and interstitial fibrosis that preserves the underlying alveolar architecture, lacking the fibroblastic foci and honeycombing of UIP. In many patients it represents a pulmonary manifestation of systemic autoimmune disease, in which immune-mediated alveolar septal injury and repair produce diffuse septal thickening and ground-glass change.
additionalDifferentials: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis presenting with ground-glass change
additionalInvestigations: HRCT thorax assessing distribution and degree of ground-glass and reticulation
Pulmonary function tests with transfer factor (restrictive defect with reduced DLCO)
Comprehensive autoimmune and myositis serology including antisynthetase antibodies
Detailed environmental, occupational and drug exposure history
Bronchoalveolar lavage where lymphocytosis may support cellular NSIP or an alternative diagnosis
Surgical lung biopsy when the diagnosis remains unclear after multidisciplinary review
Assessment for extrapulmonary connective tissue disease including nailfold capillaroscopy, creatine kinase and rheumatology referral
redFlags: Rapid clinical decline or an acute exacerbation
Features of associated connective tissue disease requiring systemic treatment, such as scleroderma renal or cardiac involvement
reference.prognosis: Cellular NSIP has an excellent outlook with treatment, whereas fibrotic NSIP behaves intermediately between cellular NSIP and IPF, and a subset progresses despite therapy.
pitfalls: Labelling disease as idiopathic without a thorough connective tissue disease and exposure work-up
Confusing fibrotic NSIP with UIP, leading to incorrect prognosis and management
Withholding immunosuppression that could benefit inflammatory disease
Missing antisynthetase syndrome presenting initially as interstitial lung disease
references: Murray & Nadel's Textbook of Respiratory Medicine
ATS/ERS international multidisciplinary classification of the idiopathic interstitial pneumonias
management: Treat with corticosteroids, adding a steroid-sparing immunosuppressant such as mycophenolate or azathioprine, particularly for the cellular inflammatory subtype which responds well
Identify and treat any underlying connective tissue disease, coordinating immunosuppression including rituximab in selected cases with rheumatology
Consider antifibrotic therapy with nintedanib for a progressive fibrotic phenotype behaving like fibrotic disease
Provide supportive care with supplemental oxygen for hypoxaemia, pulmonary rehabilitation and vaccination against respiratory pathogens
Remove ongoing drug or environmental exposures identified as contributory
Monitor with serial lung function including transfer factor and interval HRCT to detect progression
Refer progressive treatment-refractory disease for lung transplantation assessment and manage complex cases through a multidisciplinary interstitial lung disease team
